baseline_models.focus_anchor: ءَامَنتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَٱسْمَعُونِ joins a first-person perfect confession to a plural imperative with fa.
baseline_models.mechanism: Settled assent to the addressees' Lord supplies the warrant for asking them not merely to register sound but to understand and heed the speaker.

activation_trace.role: Heart-settling assent supplies the settled confession from which the appeal proceeds.
Lordship as ownership and sovereignty identifies the authority confessed.
Hearing as understanding and compliance turns the imperative into a demand for responsive uptake.

changed_reading.before: I believe in your Lord; hear the fact.
changed_reading.after: My settled assent to your Lord warrants a demand that you understand and heed what I say.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The branch range of ءَامَنتُ and رَبِّكُمْ permits trust-security and sustaining lordship to coexist in the focus wording.
baseline_models.mechanism: Belief can be heard as entering trusting security, while lordship can name ongoing repair, nurture, and completion; the clause thus depicts entrustment to a sustaining authority.

activation_trace.role: Security and confidence recast belief as an enacted placement of trust.
Repair, nurture, and completion make the Lord a sustaining agent rather than only a title.
Responsive hearing asks the audience to consider the speaker's transfer of reliance.

changed_reading.before: I have adopted a proposition about your sovereign.
changed_reading.after: I have placed myself in secure trust with the one who tends and completes; attend to this lived transfer of reliance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: فَٱسْمَعُونِ makes the inward claim of ءَامَنتُ explicitly seek a public hearing.
baseline_models.mechanism: The utterance externalizes heart-assent as witness intended to be socially heard rather than left private.

activation_trace.role: Inwardly settled assent is the content made public.
Social audibility and circulation give the imperative a public-witness horizon.

changed_reading.before: A private inward belief is reported.
changed_reading.after: Inner assent is deliberately converted into a public, potentially circulating testimony.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated nonbelief despite warning is followed by the profile of one who follows the reminder; the man then follows the messengers and asks others to hear him. His focus utterance enacts the responsive hearing denied elsewhere.

activation_trace.role: Negated assent establishes the unresponsive communal baseline against which the focus confession stands.
The repeated negation shows that exposure to warning need not become heart-settling assent.
Following as going after a lead supplies the behavioral shape of receptive hearing.
The reminder is the activating object that calls for more than acoustic exposure.
The man's own command to follow makes practical response the immediate lead-in to his confession.
The positive first-person confession embodies the assent repeatedly absent from the crowd.
Understanding and compliance make 'listen' an invitation to become the same kind of responsive hearer.

structural_cues: 36:7 and 36:10 repeat nonbelief after warning; 36:11 ties effective warning to following the reminder; 36:20-25 stages one follower addressing his people.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated nonbelief, following, reminder, and the focus imperative; I infer that hearing names responsive uptake. A live alternative is that the imperative asks only for immediate attention.

changed_reading.after: Become a responsive hearer: let my enacted belief move you from exposure to following.

context_deltas.mechanism: Threatened pain, the alternatives' inability to remove harm or extract the speaker from danger, and the subsequent forgiveness and honor activate security within ءَامَنتُ and completing care within رَبّ.

activation_trace.role: Punitive torment supplies the coercive setting in which the focus confession is made.
Pain makes security an immediate practical issue rather than an abstract association.
Harm opposed to benefit names the danger against which objects of reliance are tested.
Extraction from a predicament supplies the rescue capacity explicitly denied to the alternative gods.
Security and confidence turn the confession into a transfer of protection under pressure.
Nurture and completion identify the trusted Lord as the agent who carries a life to its proper end.
Protective covering of fault supplies the first stated outcome of the speaker's relation to his Lord.
The shift to 'my Lord' personalizes the completing care activated in the focus.
Honor and noble regard complete the reversal from threatened humiliation.

structural_cues: The threat in 36:18 precedes the speaker's rescue test in 36:23; 36:26-27 follows the focus immediately with entry, forgiveness, and honor.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies threatened pain, failed alternative rescue, focus ءامن, and subsequent forgiveness and honor; I infer a transfer of protection to the Lord. Alternatively ءامن may remain ordinary assent with security only a lexical echo.

changed_reading.before: I assent to your Lord despite danger.
changed_reading.after: Under threatened pain, I place my security with the Lord whose care is then shown as forgiveness and honored completion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The messengers define their work as delivery; the man moves purposefully from the city's edge, urges people to follow them, and then solicits hearing. A recipient of the message becomes its local relay without becoming an official messenger.

activation_trace.role: The messenger-message relation establishes the communication chain entering the town.
Delivery of a message identifies successful arrival at hearers as the messengers' stated task.
Purposeful movement carries the received message from the city's edge into public address.
Following links the citizen's appeal directly back to those who bore the message.
The named messengers remain the source whose message the citizen relays.
The demand for receptive hearing makes the citizen an active local link in delivery.

structural_cues: 36:13-17 introduces messengers and clear delivery; 36:20-25 transfers the speaking initiative to a man from the city.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a delivery chain, purposeful arrival, endorsement, and the focus hearing command; I infer relay from recipient to neighbors. The alternative is simple endorsement with no retransmission role.

changed_reading.before: A townsman states his individual belief.
changed_reading.after: A recipient becomes a local relay: he carries the messengers' communication into his own public testimony and asks for uptake.

context_deltas.mechanism: The explicit address to 'my people' before the focus, the unmarked plural 'your Lord/listen to me' in it, and the renewed 'my people' afterward allow the focus to hinge between two audiences: the town or the messengers.

activation_trace.role: The messengers' 'our Lord' supplies a prior shared-sovereignty formula that can receive the man's confession.
The named human collective marks the man's explicit audience before the focus.
The second-person plural possessive attaches sovereignty to whichever audience the unmarked pronoun selects.
The plural command establishes an audience while leaving its local identity unstated.
The renewed 'my people' keeps the town as the desired ultimate recipients after the focus.
Desired disclosure to the people preserves the communicative aim even if the focus briefly turns toward the messengers.

structural_cues: The vocative يَٰقَوْمِ occurs in 36:20 but not in 36:25; the focus uses two second-person plurals, and 36:26 again names قَوْمِى.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the vocative pattern and pronoun shifts; I infer an audience hinge. Continuous address to the town remains equally live, while a turn to the messengers would make 'listen' a request to receive or witness the confession.

changed_reading.before: He simply continues addressing the town.
changed_reading.after: The clause can face the town ('your own Lord; heed me') or turn to the messengers ('I believe in your Lord; receive my confession'), with his people still the ultimate hoped-for hearers.

context_deltas.mechanism: The voluntary imperative to hear is followed by a single frightening cry that stills the town; later single cries overtake disputants and gather everyone. Chosen responsive hearing is set against sound that compels cessation and assembly.

activation_trace.role: Understanding and compliance define the voluntary auditory response still open in the focus.
The frightening cry replaces the man's solicited speech with an overwhelming sound event.
Life or awareness stilled after motion supplies the terminal result of refusing the earlier opening.
The repeated frightening cry generalizes the replacement of deliberative hearing by sudden seizure.
Ongoing dispute marks speech that persists until the cry involuntarily interrupts it.
A third single-cry occurrence confirms the surah-wide auditory sequence.
Gathering the dispersed supplies the compelled collective response produced by the later cry.

structural_cues: 36:29 follows the focus by four ayat; 36:49 and 36:53 repeat the formula of one cry, moving from a town's stilling to universal gathering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the hearing imperative and repeated one-cry sequence; I infer a contrast between voluntary uptake and involuntary auditory compulsion. The cries may instead function only as sudden-event markers with no intended answer to the man's plea.

changed_reading.before: Listen while I make my case.
changed_reading.after: Listen responsively while hearing remains voluntary, before overwhelming sound ends dispute and compels the collective response.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it treats a brief spoken imperative as a durable trace across scenes. It remains anchored in سمع's social circulation, while 36:12 records transmitted or remaining آثار and 36:26 preserves the speaker's wish that his people know. Render it as a whole-surah possibility, not as a claim that أثر explicitly denotes this utterance.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: فَٱسْمَعُونِ seeks social audibility for the confession rather than leaving it in the speaker's heart.

activation_trace.role: Recorded establishment supplies a durable register in which acts and effects can persist.
A report transmitted until it becomes received tradition supplies the possible afterlife of audible testimony.
A remaining mark supplies the durable-effect side of the same speech trace.
Social circulation anchors the outlier directly in the focus hearing command.
The wish for disclosure to his people keeps the confession oriented toward knowledge beyond its first hearing.

changed_reading.before: Hear me in this immediate encounter.
changed_reading.after: Let this confession become a transmitted, remaining trace through which my people may yet come to know.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links distant judgment imagery to the focus and shifts persuasion toward forensic witness. It remains anchored in the voluntary first-person confession and command to hear, while 36:65 seals mouths and redirects intelligible testimony to limbs. Render it as a structural echo, not as a claim that 36:25 explicitly predicts bodily testimony.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ءَامَنتُ ... فَٱسْمَعُونِ is a voluntary, mouth-led first-person witness offered for hearing.

activation_trace.role: Settled assent supplies the content voluntarily witnessed by the speaker.
Ordinary auditory reception anchors the offered oral testimony.
A preventing seal closes the later voluntary mouth channel.
Intelligible speech connecting speakers is reassigned from mouths to hands.
Testimony as informed declaration makes the later body an involuntary witness.

changed_reading.before: Hear my attempt to persuade you.
changed_reading.after: Hear a freely offered self-witness now, before the surah's later scene where testimony speaks through sealed-off bodies.

strongest_changes: The warning and following sequence turns hearing from acoustic attention into responsive uptake.
Threat, failed rescue, forgiveness, and honor activate belief as a transfer of security to completing lordship.
The messenger and delivery chain turns the townsman from recipient into local relay.
Repeated single cries make the focus imperative a last opening for voluntary hearing before sound compels cessation and gathering.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly changes who or what speaks and hears: messengers, a local believer, a single cry, and finally limbs behind sealed mouths. That made 36:25 an auditory and testimonial hinge rather than a standalone confession.
remaining_uncertainties: The plural audience in رَبِّكُمْ and فَٱسْمَعُونِ may be the town, the messengers, or deliberately hinge between them.
The security and nurture branches may be live lexical activation without displacing the ordinary assent and sovereignty reading.
The later cry, trace, and bodily-testimony patterns may be intentional whole-surah echoes or only reader-supplied structural resonances.
